<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**[[List of journalists killed during the War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
***[[BBC Pashto]] reporter Ahmad Shah is shot dead in the eastern province of [[Khost Province|Khost]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-43953322 (BBC)]
**[[30 April 2018 Kabul suicide bombings]]
***Twin suicide bombings in [[Kabul]], [[Afghanistan]], kill at least 25 people, including prominent [[Agence France-Presse]] photographer [[Shah Marai]] and three [[Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty]] journalists who were covering the first bombing. [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant – Khorasan Province|ISIL's Afghan branch]] claims responsibility. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-43946539 (BBC)]
**A suicide attack on a foreign military convoy in [[Kandahar]] kills at least eleven nearby children and wounds sixteen including five [[Romania]]n soldiers. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/south-asia/11-children-killed-in-afghan-suicide-attack-on-foreign-convoy-officials/articleshow/63973188.cms (''The Times of India'')]
**Two rush hour bombings hit [[Kabul]], killing four and injuring five. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/south-asia/morning-rush-hour-blasts-hit-kabul-killing-four/articleshow/63968155.cms (''The Times of India'')]
*[[2018 Gaza border protests]]
**The [[Israel Defense Forces]] say they shot dead three [[Palestinians]] in two incidents yesterday. The IDF says one was killed trying to breach the [[Israel]]i-[[Gaza Strip|Gazan]] border fence while a second was wounded and arrested. They say the second incident saw two men shot dead after bypassing the fence and throwing explosives at IDF soldiers. [https://thewire.in/world/israeli-military-kills-three-palestinians-along-gaza-strip-border (''The Wire'')]
*[[Iran–Iraq War]]
**[[Amnesty International]] and [[Justice for Iran]] accuse [[Iran]] of building over at least seven mass graves in six provinces containing thousands of bodies from executions of suspected [[Mujahedeen-e Khalq]] towards the end of the 1980-88 war. [https://www.rferl.org/a/iran-paving--mass-graves-1988-killings-amnesty-international/29200805.html (RFE/RL)]
*[[Operation Inherent Resolve]]
** The U.S.-led coalition in [[Iraq]] declares an end to major combat operations against [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] in Iraq and closes the [[Coalition Forces Land Component Command]] headquarters. The U.S.-led coalition says in a statement that it would transition "from supporting and enabling combat operations to the training and development of self-sufficient Iraqi security-related capabilities". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mideast-crisis-iraq-usa/u-s-led-coalition-signals-end-of-major-operations-against-islamic-state-in-iraq-idUSKBN1I11S1 (Reuters)]
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**Iran's [[Tasnim News Agency]] denies reports that yesterday's missile attack in [[Hama Governorate|Hama]] and [[Aleppo Governorate]] hit an Iranian military base and says that no Iranian soldiers were killed in the attack. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mideast-crisis-syria-iran/iran-denies-reports-of-rockets-hitting-its-military-base-in-syria-killing-iranians-tasnim-idUSKBN1I10IR (Reuters)] 
**A Syrian military source cited by pro-Syrian government news outlet [[Al-Masdar News]] says that an Israeli [[F-35]] killed more than 30 soldiers yesterday in an attack that completely destroyed the Syrian government's Brigade 47 missile base in [[Hama Governorate|Hama]]. [https://www.almasdarnews.com/article/suspected-israeli-attack-completely-destroys-syrian-missile-base-in-hama-photos/ (Al-Masdar News)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economy of the United Kingdom]]
**British supermarkets [[Asda]] and [[Sainsbury's]] agree terms on a [[Pound sterling|£]]13 billion merger, which could form the largest UK supermarket company. [https://news.sky.com/story/sainsburys-and-asda-agree-to-join-forces-11353408 (Sky News)]
*The [[Central Bank of Iraq]] holds a currency auction, raising [[US$]]174,367,874. [https://www.iraqinews.com/business-iraqi-dinar/central-bank-of-iraq-auctions-174367874-on-30-april-2018/ (Iraqi News)]
*[[Marathon Oil]] purchases [[Andeavor]] for [[US dollar|$]]23.3 billion, creating the biggest oil refining firm in the [[United States]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-04-30/marathon-to-buy-andeavor-in-23-3-billion-u-s-oil-refining-deal (Bloomberg)]
;Disasters and accidents
*The Mezhegei coal mine in [[Tuva]], [[Siberia]], [[Russia]], suffers a collapse. A total of 79 miners are rescued but one remains missing. [https://themoscowtimes.com/news/russian-miner-trapped-in-coal-mine-collapse-61300 (The Moscow Times)]
;Health and environment
*[[Euthanasia in Australia]]
**[[David W. Goodall]], an [[Australia]]n scientist aged 104, announces his intention to travel assisted by [[Exit International]] to [[Switzerland]] to [[assisted suicide|end his own life]]. Goodall is not [[terminal illness|terminally ill]] but says his [[quality of life]] has deteriorated with age. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2018/apr/30/david-goodall-australia-oldest-scientist-to-end-own-life-in-switzerland (The Guardian)]
;International relations
*[[Foreign relations of Uzbekistan]]
**[[Uzbekistan]] agrees to formally join the [[Turkic Council]] following a meeting between [[President of Uzbekistan|Uzbek President]] [[Shavkat Mirziyoyev]] and [[President of Turkey|Turkish President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] in [[Tashkent]]. [http://en.apa.az/azerbaijan-politics/foreign-news/uzbekistan-to-join-cooperation-council-of-turkic-speaking-states.html (APA)]
*[[South Korea–United States relations]]
**[[South Korea]]n president [[Moon Jae-in]] suggests that U.S. president [[Donald Trump]] should receive the [[Nobel Peace Prize]] for his efforts to help denuclearize the [[Korean Peninsula]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/asia_pacific/trump-should-get-the-nobel-peace-prize-for-north-korea-talks-says-souths-moon/2018/04/30/9f89798c-4c6d-11e8-b966-bfb0da2dad62_story.html?noredirect=on (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[China–North Korea relations]] 
**[[China|Chinese]] diplomat [[Wang Yi (politician)|Wang Yi]] will travel to [[North Korea]] to meet with [[Kim Jong-un]] following the [[April 2018 inter-Korean summit|summit]]. [https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2018/04/30/Chinas-top-diplomat-to-travel-to-North-Korea/7031525106755/ (Upi)]
*[[Ukraine–United States relations]]
**The [[United States Department of State|U.S. State Department]] confirms the U.S. has completed a delivery of [[FGM-148 Javelin]] anti-tank missile systems to [[Ukraine]]. [https://www.rferl.org/amp/javelin-missile-delivery-ukraine-us-confirmed/29200588.html (RFE/RL)]
*[[2018 North Korea–United States summit]]
**The summit is considering to take place at the [[Inter-Korean Peace House|Peace House]] at the DMZ, where the North-South Korea summit was also held. [http://www1.cbn.com/cbnnews/national-security/2018/april/dmz-peace-freedom-house-could-be-site-of-historic-us-north-korea-summit-nbsp (CBN)]
*[[Human rights in Vietnam]]
**The [[Germany|German]] daily ''[[Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung]]'' reports that last year’s visit of the [[Vietnam]]ese public security minister and his entourage to [[Slovakia]] was used to cover for the abduction of a dissident Vietnamese entrepreneur [[Trịnh Xuân Thanh]] who had previously emigrated to [[Germany]]. [https://spectator.sme.sk/c/20815700/german-media-vietnam-kidnapping-throughout-slovakia.html (''The Slovak Spectator'')]
*[[Poland in the European Union]]
**[[Poland|Polish]] Foreign Minister [[Jacek Czaputowicz]] says the nation will oppose [[European Union]] budget rules set to be introduced on May 2 by the [[European Commission]]. The proposals would see funding in the 2021-2027 budget cut for countries where democratic principles and the rule of law are deemed under threat. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/europe/ap-interview-poland-against-eu-linking-funds-to-rule-of-law/2018/04/30/4b1f1814-4c6a-11e8-85c1-9326c4511033_story.html?noredirect=on&utm_term=.eedcbfc7ac36 (The Washington Post)]
*[[Japan–United States relations]]
**[[Japan]] lodges a formal complaint after footage appears on [[YouTube]] of a [[US]] [[F-16]] [[fighter jet]] based at [[Misawa Air Base]] in [[Aomori Prefecture|Aomori]] flying at high speed and low altitude through mountains in an apparent breach of regulations. Japanese law prohibits aircraft from descending below 150 feet in non-residential areas. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2018/04/30/japan-complains-us-youtube-footage-emerges-fighter-jet-breaking/ (The Telegraph)]
*[[Brexit negotiations]]
**The [[UK]] [[House of Lords]] approves amendments to the [[European Union (Withdrawal) Bill]] in defiance of the government, adding requirements for [[UK Parliament|Parliament]] to have a final say on negotiations with the [[European Union]] and provisions for the families of existing migrants to join them in the UK. [http://home.bt.com/news/uk-news/peers-warned-against-thwarting-will-of-the-people-after-brexit-defeats-11364267858158 (BT)]
;Law and crime
*[[Terrorism in Sweden]]
**[[Swedish Security Service|SAPO]] arrests three in the greater [[Stockholm]] area suspected of plotting a terror attack. SAPO says the case has an international connection; local media reports one of the detainees is an [[Uzbekistan]]i citizen. [http://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/sweden-arrests-suspected-preparing-act-terror-54822245 (ABC News)]
*[[Terrorism in the United Kingdom]]
**[[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] terror suspect Husnain Rashid appears before [[Woolwich Crown Court]] in [[London]]. Rashid pleads not guilty to planning and encouraging terrorism, distributing terrorist material, and breaching a notice issued under the [[Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act]]. The charges include an allegation he posted details of [[Prince George of Cambridge|Prince George]]'s school and encouraged an attack against him. [http://www.itv.com/news/granada/update/2018-04-30/lancashire-man-denies-terror-charges/ (ITV)]
*[[2008 Mumbai attacks]]
**[[Pakistan]]'s Interior Ministry removes chief prosecutor Chaudhry Azhar from the case, which concerns the murders of 166 people. The Interior Ministry said Azhar did "not take the government line". Seven alleged [[Lashkar-e-Taiba]] members have been facing charges since 2009 but nobody has yet been convicted in Pakistan. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/pakistan/pakistan-removes-chief-prosecutor-of-mumbai-terror-attack-case-for-not-taking-govt-line/articleshow/63963272.cms (''The Times of India'')]
*The [[United Nations]] suspends Miriam Maluwa as director of the [[UNAIDS]] programme in [[Ethiopia]]. Maluwa is a key witness in allegations of [[sexual assault]] against a programme director, [[Luiz Loures]]. Loures is accused of attacking colleague Martina Brostrom in a lift and is due to leave his post today. Brostrom today said she has no confidence the UN will deliver justice as it reopens its investigation. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/europe/accuser-in-unaids-sex-assault-case-rejects-new-probe/articleshow/63974520.cms (''The Times of India'')] [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/europe/un-suspends-key-witness-in-sexual-assault-probe/articleshow/63971334.cms (''The Times of India'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Politics of the United Kingdom]]
**[[Sajid Javid]] becomes the [[United Kingdom]]'s [[Home Secretary]] following the resignation of [[Amber Rudd]] over the [[Windrush scandal]]. He is the first Home Secretary from an ethnic minority background. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-43946845 (BBC)]
*The [[Palestinian National Council]], the legislative arm of the [[Palestinian Liberation Organisation]], convenes for the first time in nine years in [[Ramallah]]. The agenda includes voting in a new eighteen-member PLO Executive Committee, transforming the [[Palestinian Authority]] into a state with its own institutions and monetary system, and cessation of ties with [[Israel]]. [[Gaza Strip|Gazan]] rivals [[Hamas]] are not invited. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/04/palestinians-pnc-palestinian-national-council-discuss-recognition-israel-180424144047076.html (al-Jazeera)]

;Science and technology
*[[Russian floating nuclear power station]]
**Russia’s first floating nuclear power plant, the ''[[Akademik Lomonosov]],'' sets sail across the [[Baltic Sea]] from [[Saint Petersburg|St. Petersburg]]. [http://www.alphr.com/energy/1009217/russia-floating-chernobyl-nuclear-power-plant (Alphr)]
*The world's oldest known spider, a [[trapdoor spider]] known as "Number 16", dies of a wasp sting at the age of 43. [https://www.yahoo.com/news/worlds-oldest-known-spider-dies-australia-wasp-sting-032111961.html (Yahoo! News via AFP)]
